def specialFilter(nums):
    
    
    count = 0
    for num in nums:
        if num > 10:
            odd_digits = (1, 3, 5, 7, 9)
            number_as_string = str(num)
            if int(number_as_string[0]) in odd_digits and int(number_as_string[-1]) in odd_digits:
                count += 1
        
    return count

def test_specialFilter():
    # Basic examples
    assert specialFilter([15, -73, 14, -15]) == 1
    assert specialFilter([33, -2, -3, 45, 21, 109]) == 2

    # Empty list
    assert specialFilter([]) == 0

    # No numbers greater than 10
    assert specialFilter([1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 10, -11]) == 0

    # Numbers with even first or last digit are excluded
    assert specialFilter([11, 13, 15, 17, 19]) == 5
    assert specialFilter([12, 14, 16, 18, 20]) == 0
    assert specialFilter([21, 23, 25, 27, 29]) == 0
    assert specialFilter([31, 33, 35, 37, 39]) == 5

    # Exactly 10 is excluded (not > 10)
    assert specialFilter([10]) == 0

    # Negative numbers are excluded even if digits are odd
    assert specialFilter([-11, -13, -19]) == 0

    # Multi-digit numbers with odd first and last digits
    assert specialFilter([111, 133, 155, 177, 199]) == 5
    assert specialFilter([101, 121, 141]) == 0

    # Large numbers
    assert specialFilter([98765, 12345, 55555]) == 2

    # Mixed list
    assert specialFilter([15, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 77, 88, 99]) == 4
